notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance ran out after 28 searches (the five legislative candidates, the county candidates and five of the city candidates were searched; Sarah Sanchez, every school board candidate and the two judges were not). Everything after that was read by opening known addresses directly with the kit's honest User-Agent: the filed campaign websites, each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's and the Republican Party of Minnesota's sites, and news pages the earlier searches had already named. No search engine was read in place of the search tool.

The nine campaign websites filed in this slice were read from the record (sl_websites, read-only) and each was opened; all nine name the candidate and the office or place. They are repeated here as website findings so the second reader checks them.

Nothing recorded, and why. Don Wachal: Jackson County's own Commissioners page names him as District 2 commissioner, but the county's robots.txt asks every script to stay out; the page had been read once through the fetch tool before the robots.txt was checked, so nothing from it is kept and the site was not asked again. Joseph P. Glasrud: Stevens County's County Attorney page and staff directory, as served to a script, do not name the county attorney. The two judges (Michelle A. Hatcher, Catherine (Kate) McPherson): mncourts.gov answered 403 once and was not asked again. Aiden VanBeck, Judson Sandahl, Mariajose Saenz, Sarah Sanchez, Janet Johnson, Monica Kunkel and Nicholas Schaefer: no campaign site is filed, and the Victoria, Worthington, Owatonna, Shakopee, Buffalo-Hanover-Montrose and South St. Paul pages of today's council or board members do not show Sandahl, Saenz, Sanchez, Johnson, Kunkel or Schaefer in office; with searching gone nothing more could be looked for. Keith Friedsam: the Perham-Dent district's site did not answer (three tries). A second pass with searching would be worth it for these.

Republican endorsement of AJ Gubash: none could be recorded. mngop.com's "2026 Republican Nominees" page does not name him; no site of the Senate District 53 or Dakota County Republicans could be reached without searching; his own site's home and About pages do not use the words Republican or endorsed.

Ages printed in KAXE's guides (Patrick Rafferty, Ron Johnson) were not turned into birth years: an age on election day fits two birth years. Marisa Ulmen: the Minnesota Historical Election Archive (University of Minnesota Libraries) shows a full birth date taken from a birth records index; it was not taken, as in other parts of this sweep. The archive is used only for her two earlier runs under the DFL label; it is a university archive of official returns, labelled secondary for the second reader to judge. What ties the archive's page to this candidate: the same name, the DFL label, Madelia in Watonwan County (her campaign site's home page gives Madelia for the campaign), and House District 22A lying inside Senate District 22.

For the second reader: (1) 'elected 2021' is written in 'from' for Abdihakim Arabow Ibrahim's school board seat because his site gives the election year and not the year the term began, as other parts do. (2) Patrick Rafferty's and Ron Johnson's offices rest on their own answers as printed by KAXE; Rafferty's two planning and zoning seats have no years. His answer also lists a year as executive director of, and three years on the board of, Cass County economic development; it is not clear that is a government body, so it was left out. (3) Eric Wallen: the county's history page says 2018-Present; his own site says he has served 'the past eight years' and seeks a third term. (4) Al Parranto: the city's page gives only the current term's dates; a North Metro TV story (northmetrotv.com/news-headlines/parranto-added-to-ham-lake-city-council) reports the council appointing him, then a planning and zoning commissioner, to an open seat, but the story as read carries no date, so no start year is given. (5) Jeffrey Boucher's official page gives no date; the start year rests on Pine Knot News. (6) Abdihakim Arabow Ibrahim's own_words is the home page's line 'Democrat running to end status quo failures and fight for greater affordability, healthcare, and safety', cut to seven words; his endorsements page lists people and organizations, no party unit, and the state DFL's page lists no county candidates. (7) Read and left out on purpose for everyone: jobs and employers, schools, military service, family, and seats on private boards and associations.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: all 25 addresses were re-opened with the kit's User-Agent and every finding (39) was found on its page as recorded, each name matched to its race in the record. Two wordings corrected: Michelle Okeson's source no longer cites the district's 2022 election page, which is not among the addresses and was not re-opened; Abdihakim Arabow Ibrahim's page says he was 'a vice chair' of the school board, not a 'former' one. The Ulmen note now rests on the campaign site's home page rather than an About page title that named an occupation. Nothing removed.
